accuracy.reason: Concurrent misses and outage fallback are accurately distinguished and supported by AWS. The card limits stale serving to acceptable product rules and does not promise free recovery.

evidence.quote: Falling back to the database is a load decision, not a free recovery path.

mechanisms.reason: Explains duplicate source work and how one in-progress lookup can serve concurrent readers; separately connects outage to expanded source traffic and explicit rejection above capacity. Given the prerequisites this is sufficient to trace both incidents without requiring a distributed coordination implementation.

evidence.quote: Many requests miss the same product together and repeat its database lookup. Coalescing requests lets concurrent readers share one in-progress lookup.
A cache outage can turn most reads into database traffic. Limit fallback work to what the database can handle; reject excess requests or serve older data only where the product rules permit it.

coherence.reason: Uses the same product, building on miss/refill, expiration, and shared-cache unreachability. The target is a connected consequence of preceding operations, rather than unexplained failure terminology.

outcomes.reason: All five criteria are satisfied. The learner traces concurrent misses to duplicate reads before refill, describes one in-progress lookup with readers sharing its result, compares 6000 requests/s with the 300-read/s capacity, caps admitted fallback reads at that capacity and rejects excess requests, and never relies on the unreachable cache. Its implementation caveat accurately marks detail outside the contract; the operational reasoning is entailed by slides 2, 6, and 7.

sourceChecks.claim: Reusing frequently requested data can reduce response latency and original-store load.
The application handles a cache miss by retrieving source data and caching the result.
Capacity eviction and noeviction rejection are separate configurable behaviors.
Concurrent uncached requests can overload a dependency; coalescing reduces pending duplicate work, and cache-outage fallback can be capped with load shedding.
